title: Who the committees with an official’s or a union’s name say controls or sponsors them
question: The City’s contractor rule reaches a committee “controlled by” the official who approves a contract. Which of these committees name a controlling officeholder on their own forms, and from when?
finding: 11 committees’ forms were read (40 statements of organization, 81 campaign statements). 4, all ballot-measure committees, name a Mayor as controlling officeholder; the 2018 committee that backed London Breed’s candidacy under the firefighters’ name names none and lists the union as sponsor. The Proposition E committee’s amended statement of organization e-filed on 2024-01-10 already names London Breed as controlling officeholder, although the Commission’s filing list shows the committee under a name without hers until 12 February 2024. 5 name a union as sponsor; ‘Supporting Our Firefighters - Yes on Proposition A’ names neither a sponsor nor a controlling officeholder.
how: Each Form 410 is read for the controlling-officeholder table (part 4) and the sponsor table; each Form 460 cover is read for the ‘Controlled’ box and the officeholder named in part 5. Scanned forms (all Forms 410 before 2025 and some after) are read through OCR. The first date is the earliest e-filed or stamped form on disk that names the officeholder; earlier versions not saved could name the officeholder earlier still. The committee’s names in turn come from the Commission’s filing list.
limits: A committee may be controlled in fact without saying so, and a form may be amended later; only the forms saved are read. NetFile prints the committee’s present name on old filings, so the name a filing carried when filed is the one in the Commission’s list. Control does not mean a gift broke a rule: the contractor rule depends on the contract’s value, its approval date and who the donor is, which these forms do not show. Unions and business groups sponsor committees openly, and a sponsored committee is disclosed as such.
